items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: the first time we heard a string bass player was Steve, a white boy who came to New York with Jean Goldkette's band.

ctx.x: Now did you -- when did Wellman Braud come in?

We never had a bass player at the Kentucky Club. The place was too small. He came in when we went to the Cotton Club, because it was only at that time the bass players were playing the tubas, but the first time we heard a string bass player was Steve, a white boy who came to New York with Jean Goldkette's band. We used to -- the Kentucky Club was just up the street, the next block, and we heard -- in fact, the whole New York aggregation, all the bands, none of them used string bass.

This guy Steve, I forget his last name, he came up with Jean Goldkette's band, up to the Roseland and was -- they were sensational! The news spread over New York, man, go up and hear Goldkette's band. New York had never heard of no band like Jean Goldkette's band out of Detroit and Steve was there, this boy from New Orleans, and he knew Braud -- at that time was just playing around New York, but he was playing a tuba and Braud told Duke, "Man, I'm going to get me a bass", that's how it all -- they were the only…
